# 2B.1 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record is **mostly positive** for 2B.1. Scholz repeatedly chose diplomacy, restraint, and de-escalation when peaceful alternatives existed, especially on Ukraine, Iran/Israel, and long-range weapons policy. The main counterweight is that he still backed sustained military aid and deterrence, so this was not pacifism, but the evidence does **not** show force as his preferred first option.

## Accepted claim items

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **Scholz im Interview mit der taz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/scholz-interview-in-der-taz-2270696 | Scholz said fear of escalation is understandable, rejected a quick endgame by force, and framed support for Ukraine as necessary to prevent Russian victory. This is strong evidence that he preferred managed de-escalation over force as the first answer. | 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.8 |
| **Questions orales au gouvernement mars 2024** | Bundesregierung | 4 Mar 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/chancelier-questions-2024-2265010 | Scholz said Taurus would require German soldiers to be involved and refused because he did not want Germany drawn into the war. This is direct evidence of choosing restraint over a militarized escalation path when a political alternative existed. | 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.5, 1B.8 |
| **Le gouvernement fédéral s’efforce de parvenir à une désescalade** | Bundesregierung | 15 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/declaration-chancelier-iran-2270888 | After Iran’s attack on Israel, Scholz and the German government emphasized de-escalation and avoiding a regional conflagration. This is clear crisis evidence of choosing diplomacy and containment over escalation. | 2B.1, 1B.8 |
| **Speech by Federal Chancellor Olaf Scholz at the Munich Security Conference** | Federal Government | 17 Feb 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/speech-by-federal-chancellor-olaf-scholz-at-the-munich-security-conference-2260378 | Scholz emphasized credible deterrence, said Germany and its partners did not want a conflict between Russia and NATO, and reiterated that no German troops would be sent to Ukraine. This is restrained, defensive rhetoric rather than force-first language. | 2B.1, 1B.2, 1B.8 |
| **Regierungserklärung von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz** | Federal Government | 26 Jun 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/regierungserklaerung-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2294518 | Scholz discussed multiple crises and security needs without apocalyptic language or reckless threat framing. This supports a pattern of keeping diplomatic channels and public communication measured. | 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.2 |
| **Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz** | Bundesregierung | 4 Dec 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/suche/rede-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2323758 | Scholz framed continued support for Ukraine as necessary for independence and sovereignty, without invoking escalation rhetoric. This is consistent with a preference for political support and deterrence over immediate force as the first option. | 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.2 |
| **The Federal Chancellor’s 2024 summer press conference “I look forward to your questions”** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040 | Scholz said U.S. long-range weapons in Germany were meant to protect Germany and NATO and prevent war, while also saying Russia had violated arms-control agreements. This is deterrence-first, not force-first, and still framed as preventing war. | 2B.1, 1B.4, 1B.5, 1B.6 |

## Counterweights / limitations

- Scholz did **not** avoid force entirely. He continued arms deliveries to Ukraine and endorsed credible NATO deterrence.
- The strongest counterweight is his support for sustained military backing for Ukraine, which shows he was not choosing diplomacy alone.
- Even so, the available evidence shows that when peaceful or restrained alternatives existed, he generally used them first and justified force only as a controlled backstop, not the default.

## Search gap

- I found **no direct 2024 evidence** that Scholz dismissed a clearly workable peaceful alternative in favor of immediate force.
- I also found **no evidence** that force was his preferred first option in the crises examined.
- The record is therefore best read as **restraint-first with deterrence and military aid as conditional support**, not force-first.
